# Finding the Antiderivative of -x^5·sin(3x)

## Method: Tabular Integration by Parts

I'll use the tabular method, differentiating -x^5 until it vanishes and integrating sin(3x) repeatedly.

| Derivatives of -x^5 | Integrals of sin(3x) | Sign |
|---|---|---|
| -x^5 | sin(3x) | |
| -5x^4 | -cos(3x)/3 | + |
| -20x^3 | -sin(3x)/9 | - |
| -60x^2 | cos(3x)/27 | + |
| -120x | sin(3x)/81 | - |
| -120 | -cos(3x)/243 | + |
| 0 | -sin(3x)/729 | - |

## Computing Each Term

$$+(-x^5)\cdot\frac{-\cos(3x)}{3} = \frac{x^5\cos(3x)}{3}$$

$$-(-5x^4)\cdot\frac{-\sin(3x)}{9} = -\frac{5x^4\sin(3x)}{9}$$

$$+(-20x^3)\cdot\frac{\cos(3x)}{27} = -\frac{20x^3\cos(3x)}{27}$$

$$-(-60x^2)\cdot\frac{\sin(3x)}{81} = \frac{60x^2\sin(3x)}{81} = \frac{20x^2\sin(3x)}{27}$$

$$+(-120x)\cdot\frac{-\cos(3x)}{243} = \frac{120x\cos(3x)}{243} = \frac{40x\cos(3x)}{81}$$

$$-(-120)\cdot\frac{-\sin(3x)}{729} = -\frac{120\sin(3x)}{729} = -\frac{40\sin(3x)}{243}$$

## Verification

Differentiating the result, all intermediate terms cancel, leaving exactly -x^5·sin(3x). ✓
